papers.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising way to mitigate task interference through expert specialization and combination. However, while existing MoE-based methods avoid overwriting shared parameters by allocating separate experts for each task, this progressive expansion incurs severe cross-task redundancy and linear parameter growth. Specifically, experts across tasks often learn overlapping functions alongside task-specific capabilities. For instance, ScienceQA and TextVQA both locate relevant image regions. To curb parameter redundancy without inducing forgetting, we propose Consolidating and Preserving MoE (CoPre-MoE). For each incoming task, CoPre-MoE first learns task-specific MoE to capture specialized capabilities. To eliminate redundancy and reduce parameter growth across tasks, we design a shared-and-private expert architecture. Specifically, we first evaluate functional overlap to selectively consolidate overlapping experts across tasks into a fixed-capacity generic expert pool. We then factorize the remaining task-specific experts into shared projection bases and compact task-specific cores within a private expert pool. To mitigate forgetting, we construct the router by pairing each expert with learnable retrieval keys, where historical keys remain frozen during continual updates while newly added keys are regularized with an orthogonality penalty. At inference, input-dependent routing dynamically combines both pools without test-time task labels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPre-MoE achieves superior performance while substantially reducing parameter overhead.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态持续指令微调要求多模态大语言模型在不发生灾难性遗忘的前提下顺序获取新能力。混合专家（MoE）架构通过专家特化与组合为缓解任务干扰提供了有前景的途径。然而，现有基于 MoE 的方法虽然通过为每个任务分配独立专家来避免覆盖共享参数，但这种渐进式扩展会带来严重的跨任务冗余和参数线性增长。具体而言，跨任务的专家常常在任务特定能力之外学习到重叠的功能。例如，ScienceQA 和 TextVQA 都需要定位相关图像区域。为在不引发遗忘的前提下抑制参数冗余，我们提出 Consolidating and Preserving MoE（CoPre-MoE）。对于每个新到来的任务，CoPre-MoE 首先学习任务特定的 MoE 以捕获专门能力。为消除冗余并减少跨任务的参数增长，我们设计了共享-私有专家架构。具体而言，我们首先评估功能重叠，以选择性地将跨任务的重叠专家整合到一个固定容量的通用专家池中。随后，我们将剩余的任务特定专家分解为共享投影基和私有专家池中的紧凑任务特定核心。为缓解遗忘，我们通过为每个专家配对一个可学习检索键来构建路由器，其中历史键在持续更新过程中保持冻结，而新增键则施加正交性惩罚进行正则化。在推理时，依赖输入的动态路由无需测试时任务标签即可组合两个专家池。大量实验表明，CoPre-MoE 在取得更优性能的同时大幅降低了参数开销。
papers.tldr_zh: CoPre-MoE 通过共享-私有专家架构整合跨任务重叠专家并分解任务特定专家，结合冻结检索键路由，在多模态持续指令微调中减少参数冗余并缓解遗忘。

papers.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
papers.abstract_en: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations. For evaluation, we adapt IoU-based metrics from object detection and propose a more tolerant alternative based on center-distance matching. Using this benchmark, we evaluate open-source and proprietary vision-language models under a direct single-pass setting, as well as settings with auxiliary components (OCR and character grounding) coordinated via pipelining or agentic harnessing. Results show that even top-tier proprietary models perform surprisingly poorly in the single-pass setting, while pipelining and agentic harnessing yield meaningful improvements. Notably, an error-type-based multi-agent workflow achieves the best performance, establishing it as the strongest baseline for future G-CGEC research. Through ablations and fine-grained analysis, we find the task remains far from solved, with linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding as the primary bottlenecks. This underscores the need for models that better integrate visual perception with linguistic reasoning and visual grounding.
papers.abstract_zh: 中文语法纠错（CGEC）通常被表述为文本到文本的问题。虽然这适用于数字文本，但在真实 K-12 教育场景中该表述存在不足，因为 AI 辅助纠错被期望直接在作文图像上进行，而这些图像主要是手写且存在许多不规范之处。为弥合这一差距，我们引入 Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction（G-CGEC），这是一个图像到定位编辑的任务，要求系统同时预测纠错内容及其在作文图像上的位置。我们提出 G-CGEC-Eval，一个包含真实 K-12 中文作文图像及细粒度标注的基准。在评估方面，我们改编了目标检测中基于 IoU 的指标，并提出了一种基于中心距离匹配的更宽容的替代指标。利用该基准，我们在直接单次通过设置下，以及在通过流水线或智能体编排协调辅助组件（OCR 和字符定位）的设置下，评估了开源和专有视觉语言模型。结果表明，即使是顶级专有模型在单次通过设置下表现也出奇地差，而流水线和智能体编排带来了有意义的提升。值得注意的是，基于错误类型的多智能体工作流取得了最佳性能，成为未来 G-CGEC 研究的最强基线。通过消融和细粒度分析，我们发现该任务仍远未解决，语言错误发现和字符级定位是主要瓶颈。这凸显了需要更好地整合视觉感知与语言推理及视觉定位的模型。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出图像到定位编辑的 G-CGEC 任务及 G-CGEC-Eval 基准，发现单次通过下模型表现差，基于错误类型的多智能体工作流最佳，主要瓶颈为语言错误发现与字符级定位。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under 4 years the field has moved from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and to proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. This survey reviews 88 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. We follow a VLA through its life cycle, from model design to training and deployment, along seven axes. Model design covers (a) inputs and memory, what the model observes; (b) architecture, how its pipeline is built; (c) action output, how it produces motor commands; and (d) intermediate predictions, what else it predicts, from reasoning steps to future observations. Training covers (e) pretraining data, the mix of robot, web, human and simulated data, and (f) post-training, adaptation to the target robot. Deployment covers (g) real-time execution, keeping pace with the robot. We analyse 22 models on these axes and report their training data, model size, inference speed and hardware. Three trends emerge: (i) training data has broadened, from about 10,000 hours of teleoperated robot data ($π_0$) to 23,000 community-collected episodes (SmolVLA) and 20,000 hours of egocentric human video (GR00T N1.7); (ii) model sizes have split: most recent models have 3-7 billion parameters, while a new group under one billion runs on consumer GPUs; and (iii) generalist VLAs are emerging that handle both manipulation and navigation, such as UniVLA and Qwen-VLA. We also compare VLAs with world-action models, which predict future observations as well as actions. We review evidence that some VLAs with near-perfect benchmark scores fail when objects or the camera move slightly, and open up further research questions.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型将网络预训练的视觉-语言模型适配为输出机器人动作，从而将网络知识迁移到物理控制中。在不到 4 年的时间里，该领域已从首个 VLA 模型 RT-2 发展到可在单张消费级 GPU 上微调的开源模型，以及能够清理未见过的家庭的专有通用模型。本综述回顾了 2022 年 12 月至 2026 年 10 月的 88 项工作，主要涉及操作与导航，另包括人形控制、世界-动作模型和评估。我们沿七个轴心追踪 VLA 从模型设计到训练与部署的整个生命周期。模型设计涵盖（a）输入与记忆，即模型观察到什么；（b）架构，即其流水线如何构建；（c）动作输出，即如何产生运动指令；以及（d）中间预测，即还预测什么，从推理步骤到未来观测。训练涵盖（e）预训练数据，即机器人、网络、人类和仿真数据的混合，以及（f）后训练，即对目标机器人的适配。部署涵盖（g）实时执行，即与机器人保持同步。我们在这七个轴心上分析了 22 个模型，并报告了它们的训练数据、模型规模、推理速度和硬件。由此浮现三个趋势：（i）训练数据已拓宽，从约 10,000 小时的遥操作机器人数据（$π_0$）到 23,000 个社区收集的片段（SmolVLA）和 20,000 小时的第一人称人类视频（GR00T N1.7）；（ii）模型规模出现分化：大多数近期模型具有 3-7 亿参数，而一组新的十亿参数以下模型可在消费级 GPU 上运行；（iii）正在出现同时处理操作与导航的通用 VLA，如 UniVLA 和 Qwen-VLA。我们还比较了 VLA 与世界-动作模型，后者同时预测未来观测和动作。我们回顾了有证据表明一些基准分数近乎完美的 VLA 在物体或相机轻微移动时会失败，并提出了进一步的研究问题。
papers.tldr_zh: 综述 88 项 VLA 工作，沿输入记忆、架构、动作输出、中间预测、预训练数据、后训练和实时执行七个轴心分析 22 个模型，总结数据拓宽、规模分化与通用 VLA 涌现三大趋势。

papers.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
papers.abstract_en: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the linguistic structure that drives typing, so every keystroke is inferred from the muscle signal alone. We propose a fully causal, zero-lookahead sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model (SSM), in which a single model decodes a whole session without windowed partitions, conditioned on what has already been typed. We achieve this by fusing a traditional typing decoder with an efficient autoregressive language model, instilling both sEMG and linguistic understanding in one model. To train such a model for per-character typing rather than whole-word text, we introduce a retokenization method that rewrites ordinary prose as human-like typing, with keystrokes, typos, backspaces and line breaks included, converting WikiText into a large typing corpus where none existed. Our model, having never seen a single sEMG-to-character transcript in typing, achieves a state-of-the-art character error rate of 25.13% on emg2qwerty's cross-user benchmark, a 5.4% relative improvement over the previous best with 6.7 times fewer parameters, while running strictly causally with no future context.
papers.abstract_zh: 来自手腕的表面肌电（sEMG）可以在没有键盘的情况下恢复输入的文本。这通常被表述为信号推断问题：从肌肉信号中读出字符并离线报告字符错误率。我们认为这种表述去掉了问题的大部分。解码器同时受到肌肉、正在输入的语言以及输入行为（如拼写错误、更正、退格和换行）的约束，而一个可用的系统必须在手持续移动的同时实时预测按键。现有系统在两方面存在不足：（1）它们以固定窗口处理 sEMG，窗口之间不传递任何信息，丢弃了会话中累积的上下文；（2）它们缺乏对驱动输入的 linguistic 结构的任何理解，因此每次击键仅从肌肉信号推断。我们提出一种完全因果、零前瞻的 sEMG 输入解码器，构建于状态空间模型（SSM）之上，其中单个模型无需窗口划分即可解码整个会话，并以已输入内容为条件。我们通过将传统输入解码器与高效自回归语言模型融合来实现这一点，在一个模型中同时灌输 sEMG 和语言理解。为训练这样一个面向逐字符输入而非整词文本的模型，我们引入一种重分词方法，将普通散文改写为类人输入，包含击键、拼写错误、退格和换行，将 WikiText 转换为一个此前不存在的大型输入语料库。我们的模型在从未见过任何 sEMG 到字符转录的输入数据的情况下，在 emg2qwerty 的跨用户基准上取得了 25.13% 的最先进字符错误率，相较此前最佳相对提升 5.4%，参数量少 6.7 倍，同时严格因果运行且不使用未来上下文。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于状态空间模型的完全因果零前瞻 sEMG 输入解码器，融合输入解码器与自回归语言模型，并通过重分词构建输入语料，在 emg2qwerty 跨用户基准上以更少参数取得 25.13% 字符错误率。

papers.title: DRA-HTR: Disentangling Representation and Adaptation for Handwritten Text Recognition
papers.abstract_en: Handwritten text recognition (HTR), particularly when applied to historical documents, remains challenging due to the scarcity of annotated data and the substantial domain shifts caused by variations in handwriting styles, document degradation, acquisition conditions, and linguistic characteristics. While large amounts of unlabeled target-domain data are often available, effectively exploiting them requires adaptation strategies tailored to the specific requirements of HTR. We propose DRA-HTR, an unsupervised generative domain adaptation pipeline specifically designed for HTR and built upon the DRANet framework. The proposed approach combines source-domain pretraining, unsupervised adaptation to the visual characteristics of the target domain, relying on the generation of target-style source samples for task-specific training. We further investigate the integration of post-HTR correction to complement visual adaptation with language adaptation, relying on large language models, which we introduce as DRAL-HTR. The proposed framework is evaluated across seven HTR datasets spanning four languages, using a single set of hyperparameters for all source-target combinations. The recognition model achieves state-of-the-art performance on four datasets and competitive results on the remaining three. In addition, the proposed DRA-HTR establishes a new state-of-the-art for domain adaptation across all seven datasets and substantially improves overall robustness and training stability compared to the original DRANet framework: it reduces the Character Error Rate (CER) in average by 13.52 percentage points, and the average standard deviation decreases from 7.23 to 1.11 percentage points. Finally, post-HTR correction further reduces the CER by 2.16 percentage points.
papers.abstract_zh: 手写文本识别（HTR），尤其是应用于历史文档时，由于标注数据稀缺以及手写风格、文档退化、采集条件和语言特征变化造成的显著域偏移，仍然具有挑战性。虽然通常可获得大量未标注的目标域数据，但有效利用它们需要针对 HTR 特定需求定制的适配策略。我们提出 DRA-HTR，一种专为 HTR 设计、构建于 DRANet 框架之上的无监督生成式域适配流水线。所提方法结合源域预训练、对目标域视觉特征的无监督适配，依赖生成目标风格的源样本来进行任务特定训练。我们进一步研究了后 HTR 校正的集成，以基于大语言模型的语言适配补充视觉适配，并将其作为 DRAL-HTR 引入。所提框架在涵盖四种语言的七个 HTR 数据集上评估，所有源-目标组合使用同一组超参数。识别模型在四个数据集上取得最先进性能，在其余三个上取得有竞争力的结果。此外，所提 DRA-HTR 在所有七个数据集上建立了域适配的新最先进水平，并相较原始 DRANet 框架大幅提升了整体鲁棒性和训练稳定性：平均字符错误率（CER）降低 13.52 个百分点，平均标准差从 7.23 降至 1.11 个百分点。最后，后 HTR 校正进一步将 CER 降低 2.16 个百分点。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于 DRANet 的无监督生成式域适配流水线 DRA-HTR，结合源域预训练与目标风格样本生成，并在七个数据集上以统一超参数将平均 CER 降低 13.52 个百分点，后校正再降 2.16 个百分点。

papers.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 Gamer，一个面向复杂交互环境中长时程任务的通用智能体框架。其端到端架构结合了感知、记忆管理与多步推理。共享的训练与部署流水线支持与常规 2D 图形界面以及复杂 3D 模拟世界进行交互。我们首先在由数万小时设备级键盘与鼠标交互构建的数据集上进行持续预训练。这些轨迹覆盖模拟游戏与具身环境，使模型能够学习物理与虚拟领域中的环境动态。随后，稀疏思考指令微调在保留复杂决策所需推理的同时，大幅减少冗余计算。我们采用一种稳定的多轮强化学习方法训练策略以进行长时程交互，该方法应对有限上下文窗口、累积的 rollout 误差与稀疏奖励问题。为实现实时交互，一个云边推理引擎可并发服务大量模拟游戏环境，支持无界上下文执行，并保持较低的在线推理延迟。在多个具有挑战性的 3D 开放世界游戏中，Gamer 展现出与熟练玩家相当的稳健泛化能力与运行效率。它在一系列常规 2D 游戏基准上也取得了有竞争力的结果。这些结果表明，即使是重复性的键盘与鼠标轨迹，也能通过扩展数据与学习算法带来显著收益。在这些轨迹上训练有助于 Gamer 在兼具物理与数字属性的环境中更稳定地学习复杂技能。该方法为能够在数字与物理世界间交互的通用智能体提供了一条路径。
papers.tldr_zh: Gamer 通过数万小时键鼠交互轨迹的持续预训练、稀疏思考指令微调与多轮强化学习，结合云边推理引擎，在 3D 开放世界游戏和 2D 游戏基准上实现与熟练玩家相当的泛化与效率。

papers.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is a multi-objective control problem that requires reducing charging time and sustaining high energy throughput while suppressing accelerated degradation and safety-critical electrochemical reactions. Conventional protocols are easy to implement but have limited ability to adapt to variations in battery chemistry, operating conditions, and aging state. Model-based optimization and conventional data-driven control often require accurate models, costly iterative search, or task-specific policies. We develop a large language model (LLM)-empowered intelligent agent for adaptive battery fast-charging control. In this closed-loop framework, the agent interprets structured battery states, generates executable charging actions, observes the resulting battery response, and continuously adjusts subsequent decisions. We construct a large-scale simulation corpus with PyBaMM across five battery chemistries and 11 parameter sets and convert the resulting state-action-response trajectories into structured process data for agent training. Our two-stage strategy combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). SFT establishes battery-control semantics and feasible decision priors from simulation-derived demonstrations. GRPO aligns the agent with a multi-objective control objective covering energy throughput, degradation mitigation, and operational constraints. Closed-loop simulations show that, under matched energy-throughput requirements, the agent achieves longer cycling life than conventional charging baselines and optimization-based strategies across heterogeneous battery configurations. This study provides a simulation-grounded proof of concept for using LLM agents as sequential decision makers in battery management and takes a step toward language-model-enabled control of physical energy systems.
papers.abstract_zh: 锂离子电池快充是一个多目标控制问题，需要在缩短充电时间、维持高能量吞吐的同时，抑制加速退化与安全关键的電化学副反应。常规协议易于实现，但适应电池化学体系、运行条件与老化状态变化的能力有限。基于模型的优化与常规数据驱动控制往往需要精确模型、昂贵的迭代搜索或任务特定策略。我们开发了一种由大语言模型（LLM）赋能的智能体，用于自适应电池快充控制。在该闭环框架中，智能体解释结构化电池状态、生成可执行充电动作、观察电池响应并持续调整后续决策。我们利用 PyBaMM 构建了覆盖五种电池化学体系与 11 组参数集的大规模仿真语料，并将生成的状态-动作-响应轨迹转换为结构化过程数据用于智能体训练。我们的两阶段策略结合了监督微调（SFT）与组相对策略优化（GRPO）。SFT 从仿真演示中建立电池控制语义与可行决策先验。GRPO 使智能体与涵盖能量吞吐、退化缓解与运行约束的多目标控制目标对齐。闭环仿真表明，在匹配能量吞吐要求的条件下，该智能体在异构电池配置上实现了比常规充电基线与基于优化的策略更长的循环寿命。本研究为将 LLM 智能体用作电池管理中的序贯决策者提供了基于仿真的概念验证，并朝着语言模型赋能的物理能源系统控制迈出一步。
papers.tldr_zh: 该工作用 PyBaMM 构建多化学体系仿真语料，经 SFT 与 GRPO 训练 LLM 智能体进行闭环快充决策，在匹配能量吞吐下实现比常规与优化基线更长的循环寿命。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model

papers.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlash, a simple and effective framework that adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly. For long video inputs, MMFlash further employs sparse attention to reduce redundant attention computation and improve drafting quality. Across various multimodal benchmarks, MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to $3.58\times$, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%, respectively.
papers.abstract_zh: 推测解码通过让轻量草稿模型提出 token 并由目标模型并行验证来加速生成。DFlash 等扩散草稿器在单次前向传播中提出整个 token 块，但主要关注纯文本任务，多模态草稿尚未得到充分探索。为研究这一设定，我们首先引入一种基于有无视觉输入时下一 token 分布之间 KL 散度的 token 级视觉依赖度量。我们发现，接受率从视觉依赖最低四分位的 46% 降至最高四分位的 22%，且这一差距在多模态训练后依然存在。受此观察启发，我们提出 MMFlash，一个简单有效的框架，自适应地提高草稿器预测较差的视觉依赖 token 的权重。对于长视频输入，MMFlash 进一步采用稀疏注意力以减少冗余注意力计算并提升草稿质量。在多种多模态基准上，MMFlash 实现最高 $3.58\times$ 的无损解码加速，分别比 EAGLE-3 和 DFlash 高出最多 195.4% 和 17.1%。
papers.tldr_zh: MMFlash 基于 token 级视觉依赖度量，自适应加权草稿器预测较差的视觉依赖 token，并对长视频采用稀疏注意力，在多模态基准上实现最高 3.58 倍无损解码加速。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
papers.abstract_en: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.
papers.abstract_zh: GPT-6 Astra 的发布标志着机器人学新范式的出现：智能体机器人（agentic robotics）。在数周内，配备智能体框架的前沿模型在许多具身基准上达到或超过了任务特定策略。智能体机器人系统不再为每类任务训练专用策略，而是将基础模型应用于开放世界具身任务。它在闭环中运行：观察环境、解读用户意图、推理任务、调用技能与工具、验证结果并调整策略。尽管取得这些进展，社区尚未就统一定义、可靠评估框架或研究路线图达成共识。我们认为，由基础模型与具身框架共同实现的具身系统 2（Embodied System 2）构成智能体机器人的决策核心。其核心挑战是在有限反应时间、机械限制、不可预测的环境变化与不可逆后果等物理约束下，将通用推理转化为有效且可验证的动作。受此视角启发，我们提出一个同时衡量模型能力与闭环系统性能的评估框架。此外，我们识别了从数字智能体迁移到物理智能体的原则，以及实现可靠物理自主必须解决的挑战。在具身系统 2 与评估框架之上，我们展望了一条通向持续自主的研究路线图：从执行单个原语到承担长期角色，以逐步扩大的责任范围安全可靠地完成工作。
papers.tldr_zh: 该文提出以基础模型加具身框架构成的具身系统 2 作为智能体机器人决策核心，并给出同时评估模型能力与闭环系统性能的框架及通向持续自主的研究路线图。

papers.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract_en: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit for a wide range of curated tasks such as logical state preparation, logical gate design, and logical routines such as code-switching, code growth, etc. Our approach consistently finds fault-tolerant circuits for all of these tasks, each verified by an exhaustive check over faults.
papers.abstract_zh: 将量子计算扩展至实用量子优势目前受限于对量子纠错码所编码信息进行操作的电路效率。量子计算全栈涵盖多项任务：逻辑码态制备、逻辑门实现、编码量子比特上的逻辑例程等。然而，这些电路大多针对个别情况手工设计，近期一些工作在某些环节引入了机器学习。我们将该问题表述为智能体式进化程序合成：由大语言模型利用其预训练知识与工具使用能力，在电路验证器引导下，进化出一个定义 Clifford 电路的程序，以完成逻辑态制备、逻辑门设计以及码切换、码增长等逻辑例程等广泛精选任务。我们的方法在所有这类任务上均稳定找到容错电路，每个电路都通过对故障的穷举检查得到验证。
papers.tldr_zh: 该工作将容错量子电路设计表述为智能体式进化程序合成，由 LLM 在电路验证器引导下进化 Clifford 电路程序，在逻辑态制备、逻辑门设计与码切换等任务上均找到经故障穷举验证的容错电路。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining

papers.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
papers.abstract_en: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. We ask whether a better architecture, together with features specific to the target database, can deliver comparable gains from far less pretraining data. We introduce MoREGT, a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer that represents both rows and cells as tokens, adds the log-ages of rows and the names of foreign-key relationships to attention, and routes cells and rows to experts by column metadata rather than by values. A label-blind LLM agent complements the model: it reads the target database's schema and column statistics and adds validated single-row derived columns, without access to labels or model scores. On 21 RelBench tasks with leave-one-database-out pretraining on six databases, the MoREGT backbone improves on the Relational Transformer pretrained on the same databases by 2.25 points of mean AUROC and 5.83 points of mean nMAE. The agent's columns raise mean AUROC from 78.45 to 79.63 and lower mean nMAE from 27.91 to 26.98, the highest means on both metrics among the compared methods, including RT-J, which pretrains on about 400 times as many databases.
papers.abstract_zh: 网络平台在关系型数据库中记录用户和物品活动，而各平台的模式（schema）互不相同，这使得预测模型难以在平台之间迁移。关系型基础模型通过跨数据库预训练来应对这一问题，但近期的改进依赖于不断增大的预训练语料。我们提出疑问：更好的架构，结合目标数据库特有的特征，能否在远少于现有预训练数据的情况下带来可比增益。我们提出 MoREGT，一种关系专家混合图 Transformer，它将行和单元格都表示为 token，把行的对数年龄（log-ages）和外键关系名称加入注意力，并依据列元数据而非取值将单元格和行路由到专家。一个标签盲（label-blind）的 LLM 智能体对模型形成补充：它读取目标数据库的模式和列统计信息，并添加经过验证的单行派生列，且不访问标签或模型分数。在 21 个 RelBench 任务上、以六个数据库进行留一数据库预训练时，MoREGT 主干相比在相同数据库上预训练的 Relational Transformer，平均 AUROC 提升 2.25 点，平均 nMAE 提升 5.83 点。智能体生成的列将平均 AUROC 从 78.45 提升到 79.63，并将平均 nMAE 从 27.91 降低到 26.98，在这两项指标上均为所比较方法中的最高均值，包括在约 400 倍数量的数据库上预训练的 RT-J。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 MoREGT 关系专家混合图 Transformer，配合标签盲 LLM 智能体生成派生列，在远少预训练数据下于 RelBench 跨数据库任务上超过同数据预训练的 Relational Transformer 及预训练数据库多约 400 倍的 RT-J。

papers.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
papers.abstract_en: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. This issue is especially severe in low-resource languages, where weaker cross-modal alignment causes models to rely more on language priors than on image evidence. Existing remedies either require costly multilingual annotations or external translation/reward models, or intervene at inference time in ways that can distort the output language. We propose VEPO(Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization), a training-time method that transfers reliable visual grounding from English to other languages without external models. VEPO first localizes key visual evidence using English queries via mid-layer cross-modal attention, then constructs preference pairs that share the same correct answer but differ in evidence sufficiency (full image vs.\ key-region masked image). Direct preference optimization on these pairs encourages low-resource inputs to prefer answers supported by complete visual evidence. Experiments on multilingual POPE and MME with Chinese, French, and Hindi show consistent hallucination reduction and perception gains, with the largest improvements on the lowest-resource language. Analyses further confirm that VEPO sharpens question-relevant attention and that evidence-guided masking outperforms random masking.
papers.abstract_zh: 大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）取得了强大的多模态性能，但仍易出现物体幻觉——生成语言流畅但缺乏视觉依据的答案。该问题在低资源语言中尤为严重，因为较弱的跨模态对齐使模型更多依赖语言先验而非图像证据。现有补救方法要么需要昂贵的多语言标注或外部翻译/奖励模型，要么在推理时进行干预而可能扭曲输出语言。我们提出 VEPO（视觉证据引导的偏好优化），一种训练时方法，无需外部模型即可将可靠的视觉 grounding 从英语迁移到其他语言。VEPO 首先通过中层跨模态注意力用英语查询定位关键视觉证据，然后构建偏好对：这些对共享同一正确答案，但在证据充分性上不同（完整图像 vs. 关键区域被掩码的图像）。在这些对上做直接偏好优化，促使低资源语言输入偏好由完整视觉证据支持的答案。在中文、法文和印地语的多语言 POPE 和 MME 上的实验显示幻觉持续减少、感知能力提升，且在资源最低的语言上改进最大。分析进一步证实 VEPO 使与问题相关的注意力更锐利，且证据引导的掩码优于随机掩码。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出训练时方法 VEPO，利用英语查询经中层跨模态注意力定位视觉证据并构建证据充分性偏好对做直接偏好优化，在中文、法文、印地语的多语言 POPE 和 MME 上减少 LVLM 幻觉，低资源语言改进最大。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：preference optimization

papers.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
papers.abstract_en: Knowledge distillation usually trains a compact student from scratch, which needs a large amount of data even though the teacher's weights already encode most of what the student has to learn. In this work, we explore building the student directly from the teacher's weights. We propose Concertina, which folds every group of N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block that is executed N times. Each loop step carries a low-rank correction initialized from the layer it replaces, and a per-token gate mixes these corrections, to let every token recover the behavior of the original layers from a single shared block. We further design a distillation data recipe that balances general, mathematical, academic and targeted multiple-choice data, to recover all capabilities of the teacher together rather than one at the expense of another. On Qwen3-4B, a 2.27B Concertina model distilled on 22B tokens retains about 90% of the teacher on commonsense and mathematical reasoning and 84% on average across eight benchmarks. It outperforms same-size dense and layer-sharing baselines, as well as Qwen3-1.7B, which is trained on over a thousand times more data. These results suggest that a compact model need not be retrained at scale, since folding the teacher into itself and distilling it on the right data recovers most of its capabilities. Code is available at https://github.com/myboker/concertina.
papers.abstract_zh: 知识蒸馏通常从零训练一个紧凑学生模型，这需要大量数据，尽管教师权重已编码了学生需要学习的大部分内容。在本工作中，我们探索直接从教师权重构建学生模型。我们提出 Concertina，它将每 N 个相邻教师层折叠为一个共享块，该块被执行 N 次。每个循环步骤携带一个由其所替代层初始化的低秩修正，逐 token 门控混合这些修正，使每个 token 能从单个共享块恢复原始层的行为。我们进一步设计蒸馏数据配方，平衡通用、数学、学术和定向多项选择数据，以共同恢复教师的所有能力，而非以牺牲一种能力为代价换取另一种。在 Qwen3-4B 上，一个在 22B token 上蒸馏得到的 2.27B Concertina 模型在常识和数学推理上保留教师约 90% 的能力，在八个基准上平均保留 84%。它优于同尺寸的稠密和层共享基线，以及训练数据多一千倍以上的 Qwen3-1.7B。这些结果表明紧凑模型无需大规模重训练，因为将教师折叠进自身并在合适数据上蒸馏即可恢复其大部分能力。代码见 https://github.com/myboker/concertina。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 Concertina，将每 N 个相邻教师层折叠为一个执行 N 次的共享块并用低秩修正与逐 token 门控恢复原层行为，在 Qwen3-4B 上以 22B token 蒸馏出 2.27B 模型，八个基准平均保留教师 84% 能力。

papers.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
papers.abstract_en: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. We further develop ParetoM$^3$, a single-loop first-order algorithm for computing stationary solutions of the resulting M$^3$ problem. Under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption, we prove that ParetoM$^3$ finds an $ε$-stationary point of the M$^3$ problem that is also approximately weakly Pareto optimal for the original multi-objective problem when the penalty parameter is sufficiently large, with explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates. We also show that this stationarity notion recovers existing optimality criteria, including approximate preference stationarity and approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, under the same assumptions used in prior works. Experiments on a synthetic benchmark, image classification, regression, and math reasoning demonstrate that ParetoM$^3$ reliably attains preferred weak Pareto optimal solutions while achieving strong practical performance. Code is available at https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3.
papers.abstract_zh: 在多个本质上相互冲突的目标上学习，需要从 Pareto 集中选择合意的权衡。在本工作中，我们研究偏好引导的多目标优化，即在多个非凸目标的弱 Pareto 集上最小化一个预定义偏好函数。利用一个在弱 Pareto 集上消失的 merit 函数，我们提出基于惩罚的 min-max-min 形式，称为 M^3 问题，它将偏好优化与弱 Pareto 最优性的强制统一在单一目标中。我们进一步提出 ParetoM^3，一种单循环一阶算法，用于计算所得 M^3 问题的驻点。在局部 Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz 假设下，我们证明当惩罚参数足够大时，ParetoM^3 找到 M^3 问题的一个 ε-驻点，该点对原始多目标问题也近似弱 Pareto 最优，并给出显式的非渐近收敛速率。我们还表明，在先验工作所用的相同假设下，这一驻性概念可恢复现有最优性准则，包括近似偏好驻性和近似 Karush-Kuhn-Tucker 条件。在合成基准、图像分类、回归和数学推理上的实验表明，ParetoM^3 能可靠地获得偏好的弱 Pareto 最优解，同时取得强劲的实际性能。代码见 https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于惩罚的 min-max-min 形式 M^3 及单循环一阶算法 ParetoM^3，在 KL 假设下以显式非渐近速率收敛到近似弱 Pareto 最优的 ε-驻点，并在合成基准、图像分类、回归和数学推理上取得良好表现。

evidence: 明确的方法贡献：we propose, algorithm

papers.title: f-Divergence Self-Play for Tabular Anomaly Detection via Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Anomaly detection in tabular data poses significant challenges due to heterogeneous feature types-mixing numerical, categorical, and textual attributes, which complicate learning meaningful representations of normality. Recent work has applied large language models (LLMs) to this problem by serializing table rows as text sequences, yet these approaches rely on one-shot supervised fine-tuning that offers limited signal to tighten the model's description of normality. We propose DiSPaT, a self-play fine-tuning framework that strengthens the model's understanding of normal data. Building on the theoretical foundation of f-divergence minimization, we derive a tight approximation connecting our training objective to reducing the distributional gap between real normal data and model-generated samples. DiSPaT operates through an alternating optimization: at each iteration, the current policy generates synthetic samples that serve as pseudo-anomalies, while a critic discriminator learns to distinguish these from real normal samples; this signal drives policy updates that progressively align the model distribution with the true normal-data distribution. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that DiSPaT consistently outperforms prior LLM-based methods, deep learning approaches, and classical unsupervised detectors for tabular anomaly detection.

papers.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. At scale, modern evaluation pipelines increasingly rely on LLM-as-a-Judge to produce scores, preferences, and critiques; in its fixed-context setting, the judge relies on the supplied evaluand and evaluation materials. Yet a reliable verdict may require evidence beyond the supplied evaluand and context---either because critical environmental states remain unrecorded in the static execution log, or because controversial factual claims require external verification. Passive judges cannot obtain that missing evidence before deciding, especially when evaluating agent trajectories, executable artifacts, or domain-specific reports. Recent work therefore develops active evaluators that seek missing evidence and update their grounds for judgment before deciding. We bring these advances together through Agent-as-a-Judge, focusing on how evaluators construct and control checking processes within the broader LLM-based judging landscape. We define the scope through evaluation-directed checks and the use of their results, covering both structured workflows and observation-driven control. We organize the design space by multi-agent collaboration, tool integration, memory, and planning, and show how these mechanisms supply the checks and evidence on which a verdict rests. We consolidate published scores and reproduce missing entries for key agentic judges; the comparison reveals uneven agentic gains and motivates dedicated agentic evaluation. We conclude by characterizing application demands and open challenges in cost, reliability, safety, and governance that condition trusted deployment of agentic judges at scale.

papers.title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap
papers.abstract_en: Training language models across low-bandwidth networks requires reducing synchronization overhead. Local optimization methods such as DiLoCo communicate only after several local steps, but outer gradient averaging and the outer update remain on the critical path. Existing computation-communication overlap methods avoid this stall through delayed or replica-local updates, which can degrade convergence or cause replicas to drift. We propose LACCO (Local Accumulation with Computation-Communication Overlap), a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global communication with local computation while applying globally aggregated updates shared by every replica, without introducing staleness in the outer update. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth non-convex objectives. Experiments on language-model pre-training with FineWeb show that LACCO consistently outperforms communication-overlapped baselines such as Eager and Delayed DiLoCo. These gains remain robust as model size scales up to 0.5B parameters and across a range of communication intervals and numbers of replicas up to 16 workers, while incurring only negligible-or fully overlappable-computational or memory overhead, which demonstrates the strength of LACCO.

papers.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shifts the supervision target from imitating explanatory text to learning a tool-grounded reasoning policy. In the second stage, ARCHER refines this policy through asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning, using grouped and conditionally gated trajectory rewards for answer correctness, tool grounding, process discipline, and trace alignment. Across five standard sub-10B backbones, ARCHER improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points on macro-average across benchmark accuracies, including gains of 8.95 points on MATH-500 and 5.33 and 5.34 points on AIME-2024 and AIME-2025. Evaluations on two additional reasoning-specialized 7B backbones further show that executable grounding remains beneficial after reasoning-focused reinforcement learning or distillation. These results demonstrate that executable supervision and reward-guided behavioral refinement provide a general and effective training paradigm for compact mathematical reasoners.

papers.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
papers.abstract_en: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

papers.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information
papers.abstract_en: Satellite edge computing distributes mobile workloads across moving processors whose service capacity must be coordinated over time. In medium Earth orbit (MEO)--low Earth orbit (LEO) networks, periodic reports leave CPU states stale or missing, making offloading sensitive to uncertain capacity and shared-destination congestion. We propose PUMA-Former, an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative offloading under incomplete information that balances completed work, service delay, and execution cost. A MEO coordinator maintains distinct-report memory and closes the loop between available evidence, capacity estimates, allocation commands, and execution feedback. Latent-delay attention weights plausible measurement-age hypotheses, and historical innovations refine CPU estimates around the latest received report. Queue-error-aware fusion incorporates auxiliary pressure while accounting for backlog uncertainty. The inferred resource moments condition a structured Transformer allocator for joint destination, partition, bandwidth, CPU, and power decisions. Bounded risk-aware calibration then adjusts workload splits to reflect uncertainty and shared destination load. In traffic-driven development evaluation, PUMA-Former increases admitted compute-work completion by 8.62%, reduces mean modeled service delay by 34.78%, and reduces mean episode-P95 delay by 71.08% relative to ATLA-adapt. It also improves completion and normalized energy over fixed-half round-robin offloading. Service gains over the learning baselines involve higher normalized energy.

papers.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer
papers.abstract_en: Spatio-temporal foundation models (STFMs) require large-scale training corpora, yet synchronized observations and spatial metadata are costly to acquire and curate, limiting the availability of suitable data. By contrast, time-series data are abundant and easier to collect. Since observations at each location form a time series, this motivates a natural question: can abundant time-series data enhance STFMs when spatio-temporal observations are scarce? To bridge this gap, we propose T2ST, a data-efficient training framework that augments limited spatio-temporal observations with selected auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model. Our key insight is that temporal pattern learning can benefit from abundant external time series, while spatial dependency learning remains grounded in real spatio-temporal observations. Guided by this insight, T2ST retrieves matched sequences to reinforce sparsely observed temporal patterns and selects reliable complementary sequences to broaden temporal coverage. Temporal relation distillation aligns relationships among historical patches, while multi-scale prediction distillation transfers forecasting behavior at fine and coarse temporal resolutions, enabling knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. Using only 10\% of the original spatio-temporal data, T2ST enables STFMs to achieve overall forecasting performance competitive with or superior to their full-data counterparts across six long-term and twelve short-term forecasting datasets. These results establish a new paradigm for data-efficient training of spatio-temporal foundation models. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/T2ST-65F3/.

papers.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
papers.abstract_en: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and Blocked. Unlike goal-only evaluation, our benchmark measures physical safety and alignment with user-specific constraints via goal-reaching, collision-aware, and accessibility-aligned metrics. We benchmark modern vision-language models and find they often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection, and safety criteria across user profiles, suggesting accessibility-aware navigation requires dedicated datasets, tasks, and metrics beyond conventional embodied navigation evaluation. All data and code open-source at https://github.com/InSAI-Lab/VLAN.

papers.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. The fundamental explainability of LLMs is elusive. Here, we build a similarity network from the input embeddings of six open LLMs and map generation onto it. The token-embedding network is scale-free while heavy-tailed, as are random embeddings with matched covariance, but far more fragmented. Distillation barely changes this topology because input embeddings are largely inherited. The knowledge space is thus deterministic from pre-training. Consecutive generated tokens are rarely graph neighbours and, in most models, no more often than in shuffled order, so generation is not a walk on the predefined network, although the tokens it visits are concentrated within it. Through the logit lens in a layer- wise manner, tokens settle late in depth in most models, and repetitive models remain confined to small domain-specific sub-graphs. These observables could serve as inference-time monitors of degeneration. We thus provide a fresh perspective on understanding LLM generation in the microscopic way from node or link prediction by graph learning.

papers.title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery
papers.abstract_en: Developing effective forecasting models for diverse time-series domains requires substantial expert knowledge, evidence from scientific literature on the web, and iterative experimentation. However, translating this knowledge and research experience into model designs requires preserving source context and testing applicability under task-specific assumptions. In this paper, we propose NeoResearch, a literature- and experience-guided autonomous research framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) as researchers to discover lightweight, domain-specific forecasting models. Specifically, NeoResearch establishes an expert-inspired dual-loop research workflow, coupling hypothesis-driven architecture exploration with iterative training and hyperparameter optimization through experimental feedback. To enable knowledge-grounded discovery, the agent autonomously mines scientific literature from the Web, extracting modeling mechanisms, empirical evidence, and applicability conditions to formulate task-grounded, testable architecture hypotheses. Furthermore, a hierarchical experience memory links literature findings to experimental outcomes and consolidates conditional lessons, guiding architecture discovery and training optimization while supporting reuse across forecasting tasks. Experiments on ten datasets show competitive performance and support dual loops, literature extraction, and memory reuse. Our code is available.

papers.title: In the Eye of the Beholder: Human Label Variation in Textual and Visual Entailment
papers.abstract_en: Human Label Variation (HLV) is increasingly recognised as an informative signal that reflects meaningful differences in how people interpret the same input. While HLV has been studied extensively in Natural Language Inference (NLI), much less is known about HLV in Visual Entailment (VE; Xie et al., 2019), where the textual premise is replaced by an image, keeping the hypothesis and label space fixed. We introduce VariNLI-VE, a dataset for studying how HLV changes between paired NLI and VE instances. We re-annotate a subset of originally neutral SNLI (Bowman et al., 2015) instances and their visual counterparts, with the same annotators evaluating both the textual and visual versions. Each annotation includes a label, confidence score, and explanation, yielding 2,250 annotations. Labels and explanations are collected jointly, providing ecologically valid explanations. Because the image may reveal information not stated in the text, one might expect disagreement to decrease in VE. Instead, we find no clear overall reduction: disagreement decreases for some instances while it increases for others. Explanations reveal further variation, as annotators can retain the same label while changing their rationale. When evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) on the paired data, we find lower accuracy, weaker alignment with human label distributions, and generally higher uncertainty in VE than in NLI.

papers.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
papers.abstract_en: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity in response to natural stimuli, but struggle to reveal which stimulus features drive those predictions. Here we introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), a method in which an LLM agent iteratively builds interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code, without gradient-based training (backpropagation). Without backpropagation to tune parameters, the agent must draw on its prior knowledge and reason over previous trials to hypothesize, hand-craft, and refine human-interpretable computations mirroring the workflow of a human scientist. LLM audits confirm the interpretability of the hand-crafted models. We first validate iWSP by tasking it with constructing transformers for canonical benchmarks such as arithmetic and sentiment classification, finding that LLM agents can successfully craft compact, accurate networks directly. Next, we apply iWSP to build neural encoding models across vision, language, and audition. In the visual cortex, iWSP outpredicts existing interpretable baselines, uncovers distinct computations across early/higher visual areas, and generalizes to unseen data. In language fMRI, iWSP surfaces a confound in the data and in auditory ECoG, it systematically discovers interpretable acoustic features that predict neural activity. Together, these results establish iWSP as a general paradigm for aligning high predictive performance with human-interpretable scientific discovery.

papers.title: A Generalizable Approach to Safety-Aware Robotic Behavior Planning with an Explicit Constraint Space
papers.abstract_en: Large language and vision-language models have substantially advanced robotic behavior planning from natural-language instructions and visual observations. However, safe manipulation in tabletop environments remains challenging because the safety constraints required for a task depend on the surrounding scene and may not be explicitly specified in the instruction. We propose a safety-aware behavior planning framework based on an explicit Constraint Space that stores reusable textual safety rules. Rather than retrieving rules solely by semantic similarity, we formulate constraint selection as task- and environment-conditioned applicability learning. A lightweight query-conditioned dual-tower model identifies the constraints applicable to the current context, which are then provided together with the original task and image to a multimodal behavior planner. To handle incorrect constraint selections and previously unseen hazards, we introduce a multimodal Safety Inspector that evaluates generated primitive plans, reconstructs the complete applicable constraint set, and provides corrective planning feedback. Validated inspection feedback is further used for test-time adaptation of constraint applicability and parameter-efficient adaptation of the Safety Inspector through LoRA, while newly identified constraints are incorporated into the Constraint Space. The resulting framework integrates explicit safety knowledge representation,context-aware constraint selection, corrective safety inspection, and test-time knowledge adaptation for safety-aware robotic behavior planning.

papers.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. To construct it, we develop a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline in which a coding agent writes exam-specific conversion code and a review page, while a human verifies every example and feeds corrections back to the agent. This pipeline adapts to heterogeneous exam formats and reduces the effort of incorporating new exam editions, enabling periodic refreshes that mitigate data contamination. Evaluating 12 recent LLMs, we find that Claude Fable 5 and GPT-6 Astra exceed 93% overall, while even the best open-weight model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, trails Claude Fable 5 by 12 percentage points. When models can additionally use a terminal and web access, they retrieve the knowledge they lack and every model improves. The gap narrows but about 4 points remain, and the ranking of models stays largely the same, suggesting that knowledge held in the model itself remains valuable even with tools. We release the dataset, the evaluation code, and the construction pipeline.

papers.title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations
papers.abstract_en: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively. Here, we propose an alternative view, building on the principle that the correlations of a sequence reflect the structure of the process that generated it. We define the autocorrelation function of a layer as the average dot product between its activations at two context positions separated by a lag. Latent variables encoded persistently along the context create slowly decaying tails in the autocorrelation, and we find these tails to grow across layers in both synthetic and natural data. In synthetic data with controlled hierarchical latent structure, this growth stems from the encoding of abstract latent variables, which govern long stretches of the input. Indeed, the persistence of latent codes predicts the qualitative structure of autocorrelations and accounts for most of the empirical measures. In real text, we take sparse-autoencoder features as proxies for latent variables, and find that their persistence correlates strongly with the magnitude of autocorrelations across datasets and LLMs. In particular, the persistence time increases with depth, as do autocorrelations, implying that deeper latent features persist for longer context spans. We complement this analysis by explicitly ablating the persistent sparse-autoencoder features and observing a consequent decrease in the autocorrelations.

papers.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
papers.abstract_en: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stage verification loop that pairs pixel-aligned silhouette critique with a zero-force gravitational equilibrium preflight. The verified world compiles into a unified solver coupling rigid bodies, articulated chains, co-dimensional cloth shells, and 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics, whose simulated rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion models through pixel-aligned structural streams. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, closed-loop execution raises equilibrium-verified world recovery from $0\%$ in single-pass synthesis to $81\%$. Controlled constitutive ablations show over an order-of-magnitude larger localized corner displacement and out-of-plane pleating in finite-element cloth than in matched rigid-plate proxies. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated trajectories increases dynamic motion-mask overlap by $2{\times}\text{--}5{\times}$ and preserves motion direction under counterfactual force reversals where direct image-to-video models fail.

papers.title: Small Is Not Dead: Distance-Aware Cluster Revival for e-means
papers.abstract_en: e-means (Bessa et al., 2026) is a recent mini-batch k-means algorithm, now part of the FAISS library, that reaches the error of Lloyd's algorithm about an order of magnitude faster on large embedding datasets. Every five mini-batches, it removes every cluster whose running point count falls below a tenth of the average and reuses its centre to split a large cluster. In the authors' ablation, removing this mechanism, called dead-cluster revival, raises the error more than removing any other component added to the moving-average update. The rule, however, considers only cluster size: it cannot distinguish a cluster that is small because it is redundant from one that covers a rare, isolated group of points, and on data with such groups it repeatedly removes centres whose removal is costly. We add a second condition, based on the distance between centres: a small cluster is removed only if its centre is close to another centre, relative to a running estimate of the mean squared error. When a centre equals the mean of its points, this squared distance is an upper bound on the average increase in squared error, per point of the cluster, caused by removing the centre. The condition costs one nearest-centre search for the small clusters every five mini-batches and adds no measurable running time. On the e-means paper's embedding benchmarks, it never prevents a removal, so the results are identical to those of FAISS. On datasets with small isolated groups not used during development, it reduces the test error after two epochs by roughly 10% to 80% relative to count-based revival, and it preserves the advantage of k-means++ initialization; on the other evaluation datasets, it stays within about 1% of the better of revival enabled and disabled. We also report two failure modes that the analysis predicts. This is a CPU proof of concept; GPU implementations are left to future work.

papers.title: Unlocking Cross-Attention in Label-Scarce Regimes: A Weakly Supervised Approach for Video Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract_en: Weakly Supervised Video Semantic Segmentation (WS-VSS) aims to learn temporally consistent semantic object masks in videos using only video-level labels. While fully supervised models successfully learn temporal relationships by means of cross-attention, training these temporal weights under weak supervision is unstable and even pushes the model below its single-frame baseline. Therefore, existing WS-VSS methods exploit temporal consistency by relying on external priors, such as optical flow. Unfortunately these cues are non-semantic, computationally expensive and noisy, degrading the supervisory signal. Instead of supervising attention weights directly or using external priors, we propose MemCAM, a WS-VSS transformer framework that learns temporal cross-attention directly through feature-space self-supervision. MemCAM introduces a CAM Propagation Algorithm that synthesizes a supervisory signal by propagating past CAMs according to patch-level feature similarities in the latent space. Specifically, we constrain their induced CAMs through a consistency objective between predicted and propagated maps, stabilizing temporal attention learning. Experiments on the YouTube-Objects v2.2 and WS$^2$ datasets demonstrate that MemCAM consistently outperforms the temporal localization and segmentation performance of WS-VSS alternatives, showing that cross-attention can be effectively trained in label-scarce video settings through internal self-supervision.

papers.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
papers.abstract_en: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint. This undermines audits of API relays, which can serve the first turns of a conversation with the model a customer pays for and silently hand the rest to a cheaper one. After such a handoff, detection of the substitute by a text classifier drops from 0.97 to 0.72 (DeepSeek replacing Claude Sonnet) and from 0.87 to 0.54 for a same-vendor downgrade (Haiku), and retraining on handoff data repairs only substitutes seen in training. Preregistered experiments trace the contagion to imitation of the history's style. History also moves a model away from its own fingerprint: active probes are not camouflaged, but when calibrated on fresh conversations they flag \emph{honest} models on long contexts at rates up to 1.00, and a standard MMD equality test rejects all nine models we test. Both failures come from comparing a history-dependent reply with a history-free reference. We propose \textsc{Lineup}, which samples references from the claimed model \emph{on the same history} and tests the audited reply by its rank among them. \textsc{Lineup} controls false positives by exchangeability and needs no fitted threshold or log-probabilities. With contemporaneous references on two closed models, its false-positive rate is 0.056 (preregistered bound 0.10), and it detects 0.81 of substitute sessions across six pairs after four audited turns.

papers.title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning
papers.abstract_en: Brain MRI can reveal early signs of Alzheimers disease (AD) before measurable cognitive decline becomes apparent. However, during the transition from cognitively normal (CN) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI), the disease-related signals are often subtle and confined to only a few brain regions. Existing Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) models learn general structural representations but do not explicitly capture the anatomical regions affected in AD. We propose Anatomically Guided JEPA (AG-JEPA), which introduces anatomical tokens that interact with patch tokens during pretraining to learn region-specific representations from brain regions relevant to neurodegeneration. Building on this representation space, we further propose Prog-AG-JEPA, which models disease progression trajectory as a conditioned latent displacement within this space. We evaluate AG-JEPA across five downstream tasks spanning Alzheimer's disease diagnosis and progression prediction. AG-JEPA improves diagnosis and MCI prognosis, achieving an 8.4 percentage point AUROC gain over the strongest baseline on CN/MCI classification and a 7.1 percentage point gain on out-of-distribution CN/AD classification on the MR-RATE dataset, highlighting its effectiveness across both early-stage detection and cross-cohort generalization. For disease progression modeling, Prog-AG-JEPA consistently outperforms all baselines on future diagnosis and brain volume change prediction, demonstrating the value of anatomically grounded neurodegeneration representations for diagnosis and prognosis.

papers.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does so more than twice as fast as the best baseline.

papers.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
papers.abstract_en: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. This paradigm broadens programming access by letting users demonstrate the rule-based behavior they want to apply to unseen data, instead of having to implement it themselves. However, recovering a program from finite input-output examples is fundamentally ambiguous, as a finite set of input-output examples is theoretically consistent with infinitely many programs whose output diverges on unseen inputs. We view this problem from a Bayesian perspective, where, given a prior $p^0$ over programs, identifying the target program means concentrating posterior probability mass on it by observing additional input-output examples. In the interactive program induction setting, the learner chooses maximally informative inputs and queries an oracle, such as the user, for their outputs. We derive a greedy query-selection algorithm and show that it terminates after $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}γ\log 1/p^0(f^\star))$ informative oracle queries, and returns the target program $f^\star$ up to approximate equivalence when no other class outweighs it under the prior. The algorithm uses a language model as the prior under a PAC-style relaxation of program equivalence, where the query-selection objective is estimated using importance sampling. On the CodeARC benchmark, the algorithm improves accuracy over the LM only agent by up to 22 percentage points while observing up to 10.5 fewer input-output examples.

papers.title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM
papers.abstract_en: Frequency-selective fading and oscillator phase noise (PN) jointly impair coded sub-THz OFDM reception. We propose a decoder-confidence-guided two-round receiver combining a {pilot-aware complex transformer} (PACT) estimator, banded linear minimum mean-square error equalization, and neural normalized min-sum decoding. PACT jointly estimates the frequency-domain channel and effective time-domain PN through interacting complex-valued branches. Decoder-derived pseudo-pilots and continuous constellation-aware confidence guide second-round refinement through PACT inputs and attention, with parameters shared across rounds. At $E_b/N_0=30$~dB, the PACT receiver achieves approximately $70\%$ and $57\%$ lower code-block error rates than the best-performing learning-based baseline in the two benchmark settings, respectively. Frozen-weight tests further demonstrate applicability across channel/PN models, carrier frequencies, and FFT/bandwidth configurations.

papers.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
papers.abstract_en: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution. To interpret these structures and the trained network, we propose a conditioned atomic response mapping analysis, revealing both the global structural descriptors and the local atomic environments that govern target properties. Overall, GaDiT establishes a general framework for interpretable generation, inverse design and structure-property discovery for disordered atomic structures.

papers.title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)
papers.abstract_en: Whether a language model's answer is correct often depends on context: the same value can be right under one jurisdiction, date, or legal definition and wrong under another. We introduce GT-FENG (General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding), the first general framework to unify contextual/temporal correctness and rule-based error attribution across law, policy, and other rule-governed domains. GT-FENG checks answers against the applicable rules and identifies documented rules that match incorrect answers. It shows that when multiple rules give the same value, the answer alone cannot tell which rule the model used. In Medicaid income-limit answers from two models, documenting the asked state's own records reduces the number of wrong answers that match only other states' values by 68-78%, and more than half of stable wrong answers then match two or more documented sources. GT-FENG provides a foundation for evaluating language models in rule-governed domains and for future benchmarks and evaluation toolkits. We release GT-FENG as an open-source Python package, gtfeng.

papers.title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance on image recognition tasks, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity over input tokens creates prohibitive computational costs for practical deployment. Token reduction methods offer a practical solution by progressively reducing the token sequence during the forward pass. We propose Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging (SWAM), a training-based token merging framework that extends the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) with two saliency-aware mechanisms. We introduce a two-step matching formulation in which cosine similarity decides candidate pairs, while a multiplicative maximum saliency penalty regulates their selection for merging. We then further use asymmetric exponential saliency-weighted aggregation, which allows more salient tokens to contribute more strongly to the merged representation. A lightweight MLP-based saliency prediction module (75k parameters per stage, 1% of backbone parameters) supervised via attention rollout is trained end-to-end jointly with a DeiT-Small backbone using a composite cross-entropy, knowledge-distillation, and saliency-alignment objective. On CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100, under a conservative schedule that reduces tokens from 196 to 100 patch tokens, with the CLS token retained throughout, 27.5% FLOPs reduction and 1.35 times speedup, SWAM matches or exceeds baseline across the reported results. Under an aggressive schedule (196 to 70 tokens with the CLS token kept throughout, 33.8% FLOPs reduction, and 1.46 times speedup), accuracy gains are achieved on ImageNet-100 (+0.23%) with minimal losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet.

papers.title: Algorithmic Opacity as a Principal-Agent Problem
papers.abstract_en: Concerns about gaming and trade secrecy, frequently invoked to justify algorithmic opacity, can also mask self-serving strategic behavior by decision-makers, who may prioritize private benefits over social welfare. We develop a principal-agent test for when algorithmic decision-making should trigger disclosure obligations even when concerns about gaming or trade secrecy exist. The test, which is anchored in decision quality, relies on two diagnostics that can be disclosed without enabling gaming or revealing trade secrets: the error profile (false positive and false negative rates, overall and for each group) and the distribution of decision outcomes across groups. These diagnostics make visible whether decision-makers align design and implementation with the public interest or instead use opacity to obscure bias, inefficiency, or strategic shirking. Strong disparities across social groups, and asymmetries in the distribution of decision errors across outcome types, should trigger rebuttable presumptions favoring further disclosure. Where ground-truth error rates are unavailable, outcome distributions across groups can support the same presumption, and a decision-maker's inability to produce an error profile is itself diagnostic. The test thus treats fairness metrics as triggers for further disclosure and extends to generative and agentic systems through analogous metrics. The framework informs differentiated disclosure regimes (staged, partial, mediated, or audience-segmented). Once such regimes are considered, the domain of justifiable algorithmic opacity is significantly narrower than commonly assumed: when gaming or trade secrecy risks are legitimate, actionable disclosures (such as training data characteristics and key system design parameters) ordinarily can be mandated without compromising innovation or enabling gaming, even for technically inscrutable algorithms.

papers.title: STaG: Human-Annotation-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Text-Based Person Retrieval
papers.abstract_en: Real-world deployment of Text-Based Person Retrieval (TBPR) is bottlenecked by the absence of textual annotations in new domains. Existing Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA-TBPR) methods still assume access to target-domain human-written annotations (albeit unpaired with images), limiting their practicality. We consider a more practical setting: human-annotation-free UDA-TBPR, with labeled image-text data in the source domain and annotation-free, unlabeled images in the target domain. This setting introduces two core challenges: the absence of cross-modal alignment in the target domain, and visual domain shifts from source to target. To tackle these, we propose STaG, a dual-path framework comprising Style-Agnostic Text Alignment (SATA) and Heterogeneous Graph Memory Alignment (HGMA). Specifically, SATA leverages source-domain data to decouple identity-discriminative semantics from machine-generated stylistic artifacts, establishing robust cross-modal alignment for the target domain. Meanwhile, HGMA exploits cross-domain semantic neighborhoods via a memory-based graph to learn domain-invariant visual features. Ultimately, STaG achieves state-of-the-art performance across three benchmarks under this realistic setting.
